stem:
Chirag must divide the $16$ cm by $12$ cm rectangle in the diagram into identical squares that fill it with no gaps and no overlaps.

Which claim correctly plans the equal segments?

options.text: Mark equal $4$ cm segments along the $16$ cm and $12$ cm sides so squares of side $4$ cm fill the rectangle.
Mark segments of length $16$ cm only, and ignore making the $12$ cm side match equal square sides.
The rough diagram of the rectangle produces identical squares even when corresponding sides are unequal.
Square the side lengths $16$ and $12$ to decide the square size.

teacher.key_rationale: Identical squares need equal side lengths that divide both 16 and 12; side 4 cm works. Ignoring one side omits the identical-square condition. A rough diagram does not create equal sides, and squaring the rectangle sides confuses the operation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite/grid as a 16 by 12 rectangle with dashed 4 cm square grid.
